title: mTuner: Accelerating Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on Multi-GPU Servers with Elastic Tensor
problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods like LoRA reduce trainable parameters but face memory fragmentation and inefficient resource utilization when distributed across multiple GPUs. Coordinating computation and data movement across multi-GPU servers introduces communication bottlenecks and load imbalance.
motivation: Enabling efficient fine-tuning of large language models across multi-GPU infrastructure is critical for making adaptation accessible, as even reduced-parameter methods require careful optimization to avoid memory waste and communication overhead.
method: mTuner introduces Elastic Tensor, a dynamic tensor allocation mechanism that adapts tensor shapes and placements to GPU memory hierarchy and communication topology. The system coordinates parameter-efficient training layers with elastic tensor packing to reduce fragmentation, overlaps communication with computation, and uses workload-aware scheduling to balance gradients and updates across GPUs.
key_novelty: Elastic Tensor abstraction that dynamically resizes and reorganizes trainable tensors during PEFT to optimize multi-GPU memory utilization and reduce communication overhead.
contributions: Elastic Tensor mechanism for dynamic tensor management in distributed PEFT
Multi-GPU scheduling and load-balancing strategy for fine-tuning workloads
System design and implementation of mTuner
Experimental demonstration of speedup on production multi-GPU servers
primary_theme: Distributed parameter-efficient fine-tuning acceleration via elastic tensor management
